sections.heading: Furnace and AC Trouble in Lincoln, and What Usually Causes It
body: A no-heat or no-cooling call can start with one failed part rather than a dead system. Here is what we look at first.

items.title: The furnace clicks but never lights
items.text: Can be a worn igniter or a dirty flame sensor. Both are small parts.

items.title: It runs a few minutes, then shuts off
items.text: A clogged filter can make a furnace overheat and shut itself down. A flame sensor that can't prove the burner lit does the same thing.

items.title: The air conditioner hums but won't start
items.text: A weak capacitor can cause this, and it is worth having checked.

items.title: The air from the vents isn't cold
items.text: Low refrigerant points to a leak, and a frozen coil points to airflow.

items.title: A new bang, squeal or rattle
items.text: Don't ignore a new noise. A technician can tell you whether it's a loose part or something bigger, and a blower motor usually complains before it quits.

tail: When it is one of these, the fix is a part. Whether the whole system needs replacing is a separate question.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong With a Central Air Conditioner
body: Ice on the refrigerant line, water around the indoor unit, an outdoor fan that isn't spinning or a breaker that trips every time the system starts are all worth a call.
If you see ice or water, turn the system off and call. Running a struggling air conditioner can turn a small repair into a bigger one.

items.title: A weak capacitor
items.text: The capacitor gives the compressor and the fan motor the jolt they need to start. When it weakens, the unit hums and won't run.

items.title: A dirty coil or a clogged filter
items.text: Dust and a choked filter cut airflow until the coil freezes into a block of ice. Thawing it is the easy part. Finding out why it got that way is the repair.

items.title: Low refrigerant
items.text: An air conditioner doesn't use refrigerant up. Low means a leak, and adding more does not fix the leak.

items.title: A fan or compressor motor on its way out
items.text: A noisy or slow-spinning motor is a warning worth a call.

items.title: A thermostat that isn't talking to the unit
items.text: A blank screen, dead batteries or a bad connection can look like a failed air conditioner. It is worth ruling out first.

sections.heading: Four Things to Check Before You Call
body: If you can do it safely, a few quick checks can save a visit, or at least give us more to go on when you call.
list: The thermostat: is it set to cool, and are the batteries fresh?
The breaker for the outdoor unit: has it tripped?
The filter: if it's gray and packed with dust, change it and give the system an hour.
The outdoor unit: clear any grass, leaves or stacked items from around it.

why: Your AC repair page promises 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year, with someone answering the phone night and day. Your contact page says Monday to Saturday, 7 to 5, and closed Sunday. Someone whose AC quits on a Sunday can't tell which one is true, and that is the call you most need to win.

The headline at the top of your homepage is a long run of keywords ending in Lincoln, Nebraska, and 12 of your 16 pages carry the same one. Google can't tell which page is for what. Your reviews say it plainly: customers describe a failed part found and fixed, and clear options when replacement was the answer. Today those words live on Google, not on your site.

So the demo tells one story on every page: what customers say about finding the real problem first. It opens with HVAC company in Lincoln, NE, and gives AC repair its own page, because that is the call people make on the hottest day.
strategy.cardsHeading: Be the HVAC Company People Find on Google

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: Where Google learns who you are and where you work.
problems: Your homepage headline is a long string of keywords, so Google can't tell what you want to be found for. Twelve of your 16 pages carry the same one.
Three links on your homepage go to pages that don't exist, and the one we traced is named after a meditation retreat, so a visitor who taps it hits a dead end.
fixes: A headline that says HVAC company in Lincoln, NE, right at the top.
Every link on the page goes to a page that works.

cards.title: AC Repair
cards.why: When the AC quits in a Lincoln summer, people call the first company they can reach.
problems: Your AC repair page opens with the same string of keywords as your other pages, so it competes with your own homepage for the same search.
Its 24-hours-a-day promise doesn't match the hours on your contact page.
fixes: A page that says AC repair in Lincoln, NE at the top, with what usually fails and what happens when you call.
Hours that match on every page once the owner confirms them, and a plain "call and ask" until then.
cards.alsoAdd: Pages planned from what Google actually shows for each search, so every page targets something people really look for.

cards.title: Contact

problems: Your contact page shows two phone numbers, one marked P and one marked C, so a visitor can't tell which to call.
Your Schedule a Service button goes to one page from the homepage and a different page from the maintenance page.

A single, plain way to reach you from every page.
